highlights.title: Here’s why the iPhone Duo’s hinge could be cracking the screen
highlights.summary: Within hours of the iPhone Duo launch last Friday, people reported that the inner screen on some brand new foldable phones was already broken. The issue was similar across many photos shared on social media: some kind of issue or crack would appear in the middle of the screen above the hinge, with…
body: Inside Apple’s first folding iPhone, contact with the delicate inner screen could cause a stress ‘hotspot.’

Shahram Mokhtari, the lead teardown technician at iFixit, has actually taken apart the iPhone Duo and has a pretty good idea about the potential cause, telling The Verge that it’s due to an issue along the hinge, where a series of gears, springs, and joints work together to let the device close flat, while also trying to avoid creating a deeper crease by giving that screen space to bend more gently inside while it’s closed.

At the troublesome spot, it appears that the flexible inner screen is pushing up against a part of the hinge. That inner screen is already “extremely sensitive,” he says — if you took a pick or a sharp tool and poked at the edges of the screen, “you’re going to break that screen.” If you look at the pictures of damaged Duos on social media, there’s often a black spot where the damage is focused on the display, and that’s where the metal is hitting the screen, Mokhtari says.

highlights.title: Learner collaborates with MIT peers to develop book of AI insights
highlights.summary: Prabha Jha used her experience with MIT Open Learning’s program for senior executives to develop AI solutions for her employer, Verizon, and to write a book.
body: Like many leaders today, Prabha Jha has been feeling the significant impact artificial intelligence is having on business operations. While the rapid evolution of the technology can bring fear, uncertainty, and confusion, Jha chose a different response: excitement. She began asking herself, “How do I become part of this once-in-a-lifetime thing?”

Jha holds a bachelor’s degree in information technology from the University of Calcutta and earned her MBA while working at Verizon, where she continues to build her career. As she looked for an educational opportunity to engage more deeply with AI, MIT quickly emerged as a natural choice.

Growing up, Jha viewed MIT as “the mecca for anybody who is in engineering and technology,” so she naturally turned to the Institute when seeking an opportunity to learn about AI. Unlike other programs that took place fully online, MIT xPRO’s AI for Senior Executives stood out to Jha primarily because it offered an in-person component that allowed her to meet and connect with peers.

highlights.title: Creator of Viral Needle in a Haystack Game Roasts Copycats With 'Find the Original Game' Mode
highlights.summary: The creator of a viral indie game where players must literally find a needle in a haystack is tired of his project getting cloned. So, he made a new game mode, where players must find the real game in a pile of fakes.
body: Thanks to advancements in artificial intelligence, it’s getting easier and easier for players to 'reverse-engineer' video games and even outright copy projects that haven’t been released yet.

It’s been a hellish situation for developers in the industry, particularly for small studios without the funds for legal backing or, even worse, single creators who made their games all by themselves.

NasNakarus is the driving mind behind Needle in a Haystack Simulator, which is exactly what it sounds like. Such a simple concept is easy to copy, and there are currently oodles of similar titles clogging online marketplaces. But he’s not taking it personally; instead, he’s poking fun at the ordeal with some well-timed commentary and a new ‘mode’ for his game.

highlights.title: South Carolina's measles outbreak jumped to Washington state 5 times in 2 weeks
highlights.summary: Since measles was declared eliminated in the US in 2000, the country's occasional cases have come mainly from international travelers—visitors from far-flung places where the virus still spreads freely — or unvaccinated US residents who return from abroad with a highly infectious souvenir.
body: In a study published this week in NEJM Evidence, Washington state health officials highlight that risk, detailing how an explosive outbreak in South Carolina reached their distant state through five distinct importation events over two weeks in January. In all, the introductions led to 26 cases among residents before officials stamped out the spread.

South Carolina’s measles outbreak began on October 2, 2025, and was declared over on April 26, 2026. Officials confirmed 997 cases in the state during the outbreak. At the time, it was the largest measles outbreak recorded since the virus was declared eliminated, but Pennsylvania’s ongoing outbreak has since surpassed it.

The study in Washington relied heavily on epidemiological data, linking cases among contacts and exposure sites. But also key to the work was whole genome sequencing, which made clear that cases didn’t just stem from one single introduction of the virus from South Carolina that then spread among Washington residents; instead, it revealed five separate introductions.

highlights.title: VisionQuest is what happens when AI really goes rogue
highlights.summary: In Marvel's VisionQuest, a superpowered robot tries to better understand humanity by getting lost in elaborate, digital daydreams in which he and other artificial intelligence-powered beings live together in a home.
body: Marvel’s latest Disney Plus series is a reminder of how much a lot of gen AI hype is just science fiction.

In VisionQuest, there is no doubt that each of the AI characters is a sentient being motivated by desires that aren’t wholly rooted in their core programming. In the show, genuine AGI is easily believable because it takes place in a reality where time travel, witchcraft, and Infinity Stones also exist. Even though the multicolored MacGuffins haven’t been featured in VisionQuest, they’re important because of the role one of them played in Vision’s origins. Were it not for the Mind Stone, Vision might not be able to think and feel in such complex, human ways, or to conjure his AI family as people who feel real to him.

highlights.title: ‘I was so sick’: is running a marathon while on a GLP-1 a bad idea?
highlights.summary: As the weight-loss drugs become more common, some runners find the side-effects challenging. Here’s what experts say. Women: was your autoimmune condition misdiagnosed? Keri M, a marathoner in her 50s, knew the race would be terrible. This feeling couldn’t be chalked up to inexperience.
body: She ran the 2024 Philadelphia marathon fast enough to earn a coveted spot in this year’s Bank of America Chicago race, one of the eight world marathon majors.

But this half marathon felt different. It was the first time she had raced on a GLP-1. Less than a week beforehand, she had taken her first 2.5mg standard starting dose of tirzepatide, commonly sold under the names Mounjaro and Zepbound, for weight loss.
Throughout the race, Keri felt nauseous, struggling to keep down the energy gels many endurance runners rely on for fuel.
“After that half marathon, I was so sick,” she said. Keri had a “severe” reaction to the 2.5mg dose and, in hindsight, wishes that she had started at a lower dose.

highlights.title: China's top-secret spaceplane can't hide in low-Earth orbit
highlights.summary: A winged Chinese spacecraft bearing a strong resemblance to the US military's X-37B spaceplane was photographed in orbit by a passing US-owned commercial satellite in 2024, and we finally have the image.
body: The Chinese spaceplane has delta wings, payload bay doors, a dark heat shield, and a rear-mounted service module with power-generating solar arrays. In other words, the design of the winged ship is, to a great degree, a copy of the X-37B spaceplane flown by the US Space Force.

The photo was taken by a commercial imaging satellite owned by a company called Vantor, known as Maxar in 2024. Vantor is one of several companies that provide reconnaissance imagery of locations around the world to the US military and US intelligence agencies. The same Earth-imaging satellites can point their telescopes at objects in space.

Lower-resolution views of a Chinese spaceplane showing the vehicle’s general shape were publicly available before the DIA assessment. A US Space Force official revealed Maxar’s observation at a 2024 conference in South Korea, but the Pentagon did not release the full-resolution image to the public until Monday, when it appeared in an unclassified Defense Intelligence Agency assessment of threats to the United States in space.

highlights.title: Artist Jane Benson Has Some Strong Ideas About ‘Frankenstein’
highlights.summary: “Is a monster the person in society that nobody understands, and that’s why we’re afraid of it?” the artist wondered while reading Mary Shelley’s “Frankenstein.” “I’m like, That’s a woman.”
body: Popular culture would have you believe that Frankenstein, Mary Shelley’s seminal 1818 novel, is a horror story of male hubris, about a mad scientist contending with the dangers of his own creation. And it is, at least in part. But within Shelley’s critique of patriarchal power, there is another voice that is often overlooked: her own. About a third of the way into the book, the narration switches to the perspective of the so-called monster as he tells Victor Frankenstein what has happened to him during the nearly two years he and his creator have been apart.

The six chapters written in the creature’s voice contain some of the most achingly beautiful prose in the whole novel. He details how he learned to understand language and emotion. How he marveled at the warmth of the sun, the blooming of flowers, the sweetness of fruit. How he grew to love the family he tenderly observed from his hiding place, and how devastating their rejection was. He explains how he came to know anger, loneliness, loss, rage—and the vengeful acts they inspired.
points: “Is a monster the person in society that nobody understands, and that’s why we’re afraid of it?” the artist wondered while reading Mary Shelley’s “Frankenstein.

highlights.title: "No human at the helm": Delaware plan would let AI agents run entire businesses
highlights.summary: A Delaware proposal to let companies be operated by AI agents would help the firms' human owners evade legal responsibility for reckless and harmful actions taken by the AI, US Rep. James Comer (R-Ky.) told Delaware Governor Matt Meyer in a letter yesterday.
body: Comer, chairman of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, told Meyer that the committee “seeks assistance obtaining documents related to your state administration’s efforts to establish a new form of corporate entity to be known as an Artificial Intelligence Company (AIC).”

Comer said the proposal is ripe for abuse. “We are concerned that Delaware’s AIC proposal could be used to protect powerful AI companies and their investors from responsibility for reckless harmful actions, while also protecting non-transparent forces seeking anticompetitive regulatory capture behind state AI initiatives,” Comer’s letter said.

Comer suggested he may propose a federal law that would limit states’ regulatory authority. He said the committee’s probe of Delaware’s plan would “inform possible federal legislative efforts including proposals to appropriately limit state AI regulatory initiatives.” Citing the Oversight Committee’s “jurisdiction to study intergovernmental relationships including those of states,” Comer asked for documents related to development of the proposal and potential AI safety risks.

highlights.summary: Today, we are announcing Genie 4, our new world model, which unlocks unprecedented realism and improves real-time interactive simulation. Genie 4 is natively multimodal, enabling audio-like music, ambient noises, and interactive dialogue to be simultaneously generated with the world.
body: The Genie 4 model incorporates and builds on capabilities from the Gemini family: Gemini Omni anchors the simulations in real-world appearance and behavior, while other Gemini models provide the complex reasoning needed to help maintain a simulation’s coherence and continuity.
With this foundation, you can set an event in motion, and Genie 4 simulates what happens next: how the world responds, how it sounds, and how the people in it move, react, and speak.

Understanding and simulating the world is a crucial aspect of building AGI. Genie 4 advances our ability to create safe, infinitely variable simulations that can help with everything from developing training environments for robots and agents to unlocking the creation of new interactive experiences.
The following are recordings of real-time interactions from Genie 4, where users use standard keyboard controls for navigation and camera control, and text prompts to steer the scene as it evolves.

highlights.title: Fantastic Fleetwood seal shootout success in Carabao Cup shock against Arsenal
highlights.summary: It’s more than 20 years since Arsenal played at Highbury but their trip to League Two Fleetwood – and a stadium of the same name – did not bring back fond memories as they were dumped out of the Carabao Cup on penalties.
body: Aaron Loupalo-Bi and Viktor Gyökeres exchanged goals in normal time but Arsenal were unable to find a winner, despite being the dominant force, as Fleetwood battled to the end. Goalkeeper Jay Lynch held his nerve to save from Bruno Guimarães in the shootout before the teenager Conor Haughey scored the winner and created a delirious pitch invasion.

Fleetwood wanted to make the occasion into a party as pyrotechnics galore were set off before the match, sending an acrid red mist across the pitch. Once the whistle went, however, the fun quickly stopped as a drone flying above the pitch forced the referee Michael Salisbury to pause play.

The two teams had to stay warm in the chilly conditions, passing balls around while officials tried to rectify the situation. Fleetwood staff looked angry that their moment in the limelight was being blighted by this. After six minutes, officials called the players to the touchline and spoke to both head coaches, before restarting play after a chat with a member of the local constabulary, concluding the chant of “Who’s the wanker with the drone?”. All good knockabout stuff.

highlights.title: Resident Evil Executive Producer Says the Series' Story Could End 'In the Next 10 Years'
highlights.summary: In an interview with Yahoo Japan, executive producer Jun Takeuchi outlined Capcom’s plans for its flagship horror franchise, revealing that its encompassing narrative has a definite conclusion — and that end could come shockingly soon.
body: Takeuchi began by explaining how the team had expanded on Resident Evil’s overarching story with every game, saying that a ten-year strategy was crafted during the planning stages for Resident Evil 2 Remake.

“The series' story wasn't planned out from the beginning; it expanded with each new game. When we were planning RE:2 and creating a 10-year branding concept, this was the most challenging aspect. If you play through all of them, I think you'll realize the meaning behind the order of the remakes,” he said.
“With the release of Requiem this year, I feel like the first 10 years have come to a close, so I think the conclusion will come in the next 10 years."

This is somewhat sad news for hardcore fans who were hoping to blast through hordes of zombies with Leon until the end of time, not to mention fans of all the other characters we’ve come to know and love over the years. And who’s to say if that means we won’t see these characters again in a new, different story?

highlights.summary: SPOILER ALERT: This post contains conversation about all three episodes of “The One About Matthew Perry,” now streaming on Netflix. At the end of Netflix’s new docuseries “The One About Matthew Perry,” director Mary Robertson can be heard saying something off camera.
body: Robertson is the first to say she doesn’t believe in things she can’t see. But having spent months with the memories of Perry told through his loved ones, she admitted to one of the people who knew him best that he was more than just stories to her after this process.

Bowick has never spoken openly about her brother’s decadeslong struggle with addiction, but now shares the full scope of Perry’s life from inside the family, including their relationship as half siblings who share the same father, actor John Bennett Perry. The series charts Perry’s meteoric rise from being a working actor to a global comedic star, thanks to “Friends” and his character Chandler Bing, and what ultimately becomes the biggest role of his life –– an advocate for addiction rehabilitation while continuously suffering from the disease himself.

She also gives new details about private moments, including repeated visits to see him in rehab and being at his bedside in 2018 after his near-fatal colon rupture. “This is it, he is not waking up,” Bowick says in Episode 3, recalling her reaction when she first arrived at the hospital.

highlights.summary: The Securities and Exchange Commission 's publication on Monday of Anthropic's S-1 form —ahead of a heavily anticipated initial public offering—has led to plenty of discussion of whether the company's quickly ballooning revenues will be able to overcome its even higher costs.
body: Across 93 pages and over 70,000 words, Anthropic’s S-1 “Risk Factors” section discusses literally hundreds of potential problems that could negatively impact its business in the coming years. Many of these potential risks are the kind of standard worries about competition, costs, customer acquisition, and potential regulation that almost any business must worry about. But some risks highlight interesting potential points of failure for Anthropic specifically and the hype-filled AI bubble more generally.

After wading through Anthropic’s book-length treatise on its greatest risks, we’ve narrowed the list to the seven most surprising, interesting, or thought-provoking potential problems. Consider this a far-from-comprehensive look that potential Anthropic investors should keep in mind.

Let’s start with the biggest potential risks: Those that could “pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity,” as Anthropic writes. The company acknowledges that concerns about these risks “have been raised both within our organization and by other researchers, regulators, policymakers, and industry participants.”

highlights.title: UK Home Office May Face Investigation Over Use of OpenAI Tech
highlights.summary: A government watchdog is considering a probe into the Home Office’s use of ChatGPT technology to process asylum claims amid concerns over the tools’ accuracy and secrecy surrounding their use.
body: A UK government watchdog is considering an investigation into the Home Office’s use of generative AI tools to process asylum applications, WIRED has learned. The potential probe follows lawmakers and researchers publicly questioning the tools’ accuracy and the government’s secrecy around their use.

The Independent Chief Inspector of Borders and Immigration (ICIBI), which monitors the Home Office’s management of borders, immigration, and customs, has asked digital rights nonprofit Open Rights Group (ORG) to share more information on the tools as it draws up plans for the topics it will inspect next year, campaigner Sara Alsherif tells WIRED. ORG’s findings come from a six-month investigation into the tools, which involved 11 parliamentary questions, two ministerial letters, and 10 public records requests that attempt to pry details from the Home Office, which has withheld details on the tools.

highlights.title: Researchers are getting tired of OpenAI gatekeeping its breakthroughs
highlights.summary: On Monday, OpenAI announced impressive breakthroughs in mathematics, computer science, and physics, along with what the company says is an evolving approach to communicating its findings.
body: Expert ‘shepherds’ will decide how best to share the latest breakthroughs in computer science and physics.

It has been a turbulent few months between OpenAI and mathematicians, who are still grappling with the hundreds of preprints unceremoniously dumped on them at the start of October. This time, OpenAI says it is working with expert “shepherds” to decide how best to share its latest breakthroughs.

All three results concern some of the most consequential unsolved problems in mathematics, computer science, and physics. Some extend OpenAI’s previous work and others break new ground. Following advice from OpenAI’s “shepherds,” each has a different release strategy. For the mathematics result, OpenAI released the AI-generated output, “leaving researchers free to organize their own efforts to explain the result.” For its computer science finding, OpenAI will also assemble an external group of researchers “to explain the result.” Physics, meanwhile, has not been released at all, and OpenAI said it will “defer” to an external group of experts about how to release the materials.
points: On Monday, OpenAI announced impressive breakthroughs in mathematics, computer science, and physics, along with what the company says is an evolving approach to communicating its findings.

highlights.summary: GPT-6 Astra tops Retell’s voice agent benchmark, while Codex helps it reach a $1.6M annual revenue run rate per employee.
body: Retell AI ⁠ (opens in a new window) is a voice AI platform for contact center operations, helping businesses build agents that can answer questions, take action, and connect a caller with a person when needed. Its platform now serves more than 4,000 businesses, with monthly call volume growing from 30 million in early 2026 to more than 100 million by September.

As Retell serves more enterprises with complex workflows, it uses OpenAI models to keep call quality and reliability high. Today, OpenAI models generate responses for 80% of calls on Retell, with customers achieving resolution rates above 80%. Retell has also surpassed 1 trillion tokens consumed across OpenAI models, reflecting the scale of that adoption.
Retell’s engineers use Codex throughout development, from researching unfamiliar code to building features and debugging issues, and GPT‑6 Astra to test front-end interfaces.

Enterprise voice agents need to follow company policies and stay within their assigned roles, even as conversations change. Retell built its vCX benchmark to compare dozens of models using difficult, multi-turn conversations drawn from real production scenarios.

body: “The fire was only the beginning of the story,” Gelber said in a statement. “We wanted to understand what happens after the television cameras leave, when families are left to rebuild not only their homes but also their lives and sense of community. Altadena’s story is deeply personal, but it’s also a window into questions communities across the country are increasingly facing.”
The film features interviews with Altadena residents sharing personal stories along with conversations with professionals on climate, economics and public policy.

highlights.title: The Free K-Beauty Way to Stop Hair Loss
highlights.summary: According to Korean hair clinic Lee Moon Won, this habit may lead to unexpected hair shedding. Here, experts break down why that might be and offer solutions to keep hair looking full and healthy.
body: It’s the great generational debate: Side part or middle part? Where we part our hair dictates the facial features we want to play up and sets the tone for our overall vibe.

But what if this defining hair feature that we spend a lot of time contemplating comes with unexpected consequences? According to Korean hair clinic Lee Moon Won, sticking to one hair part forever might be the cause of one of our most pressing hair concerns: unwanted shedding.

There are a few reasons why this might be. Wonuk Hwang, MD, clinic director at the Cheongdam Lebelle Clinic in Seoul, explains that the exposed skin where we part our hair has less protection from environmental stressors such as the sun’s harmful UV rays, and that should always be looked at seriously. Hwang points to studies that show UV radiation can cause cellular damage to the hair follicles and scalp tissue, which could increase hair shedding after severe scalp sunburn. Even though those studies don’t mention hair parts specifically, he says that exposed scalp will always need sun protection.

videos.title: Jev Course – Prefill-Only Inference & Decision Models from Scratch
videos.summary: Learn how to build high-speed decision-making pipelines for language models using Jev in PyTorch. This comprehensive course covers both encoder and decoder architectures, custom causal attention masking, and KV-cache reuse to bypass slow autoregressive generation.
body: ✏️ Course developed by Vivek Kalyanarangan.
📘 Author, Quantization and Fast Inference (Manning)
– 0:00:00 Introduction & Course Overview
points: Learn how to build high-speed decision-making pipelines for language models using Jev in PyTorch.
This comprehensive course covers both encoder and decoder architectures, custom causal attention masking, and KV-cache reuse to bypass slow autoregressive generation.
You will also explore fine-tuning techniques, teacher-student distillation, and reinforcement learning methods like GRPO to optimize decision latency and accuracy.
– 0:01:12 What is Jev & LLM Prefill vs. Decode
